Socialism poorly executed, like anything else, doesn't work. Trying to do bits and pieces of socialism in a half-assed way doesn't work. Socialism used as a boon to the free market does work. You don't seem to get that 1) free markets work best when everyone has the capital available to take part in it, and 2) the capital they put into it will always trickle up, so if you take it from the top and just keep putting it at the bottom, you create a wealth cycle that maximizes money velocity, which is what keeps a market healthy.

Also, the point of the government is to do things that the private sectors doesn't want to do, can't do, or shouldn't do. There's a lot of research that the public sector has done that the private sector was then able to take and run with into the general market (pretty much everything technology-related that you own started in the public sector). But if the public sector didn't take the risks and get the ball rolling, the private sector most likely wouldn't have been able to, because private companies are naturally risk-averse and conservative with money, which is how you maintain good financials. Conversely, the public sector usually lacks the breadth of creativity to maximize the utility and marketability of a given product or concept, so that's where the private sector excels. Without the public sector's capability of having long-term vision with the immunity to risk, you are not going to have a very competitive private sector.

A good example of this is a country like Denmark, which has a public sector that is fueling massive growth in the private sector by making certain new technologies available while promoting growth in such areas so risk-averse companies have more incentive to expand in that area. A bad example of socialism is the USSR, where they pretty much got rid of the private sector and made it all public. The system was destined to break down because the public sector is not good at dealing directly with the markets because it's slow and has less short-range vision, less innovative capacity, and less necessity to innovate. It has no risk, therefore no reason to change rapidly.

So yes, socialism does work. You just have to know how it works to see it.
